beats.what: A suited exam official seizes Bank by the jacket outside the hall and orders Lynn back to her test; she walks away and leaves him caught
Lynn is frisked and her shoes checked with the other candidates, then digs a hidden wrapper out of her boot at the water cooler
At her desk Lynn pencils rows of memorised answer letters into the margin, bubbles all 30 Section 4 maths answers off them, and palms the code whenever an invigilator passes
The letter rows turn out to be a piano piece - Lynn recalls the answers by playing them back, fingering the exam desk like a keyboard
In Bangkok the print works' phone rings unanswered, its number the one posted on a car-window advert, while students watch the clocks toward 7 p.m. and motorbike taxis wait
Lynn's paper turns to the essay section - a Mandela speech prompt that no memorised answer code can cover
Lynn fakes a coughing fit at her desk, forcing her own fingers down her throat until the whole row stops writing to stare
Warned that leaving will cancel her score, Lynn lets the proctor walk her out of the hall in tears
Pat and Grace corner the print-shop owner on the press floor and push him to run their job
Suited officials sweep the exam building by radio hunting Lynn while she climbs the stairwell, slips a door and breaks out into the courtyard
Lynn knots her hair up to change her look as a searcher pushes past her in the station concourse
Lynn starts thumbing coded answer strings into the group chat as she walks, and the alerts begin landing on the phone in the print shop
The print-shop owner slams both hands over the pinging phone and stares Pat down as a crowd of students masses at the shop gate
Grace googles the essay prompt, pulls up the Mandela speech transcript and grins - the essay is solved without Lynn
A suited pursuer comes down into the station; Lynn looks up from her phone and sees him coming
Outside the Bangkok exam centre students shout and clutch their heads as a courier bike tears away and a figure hauls himself up through a ceiling panel
Grace encodes the answers as an A-B-C-D barcode, Pat carries off the printed roll, and the orange-vested couriers are shouted into line and sent out with the slips
